label: context.reference
text:
Create another run by authoring its JSON with granted file tools and delivering an artifact through an exact interface on an active checkpoint. A visible composition operation may prepare these effects; use its actual schema and receipts. For manual authoring:

1. Record. Read the current run schema from a bound artifact (artifact-home-task-authoring contains run_record_schema.document) or a granted schema path. A source path alone grants no access. If no schema is readable, identify the missing context. The file stem equals id. Records contain {id,ee,worker,trace,status,interface_state,checkpoints,active_checkpoints}. Run trace and each checkpoint trace must be nonempty. Checkpoints contain id, run, epoch, optional interface_binding, outbound_interface_bindings, artifact_bindings and required_verified_artifacts. Interface bindings are {interface,config:{artifact_policy}}. Supply artifact_policy as {mode:"all"} or {mode:"allow",names:[...],namespaces:[...]}; bare interface strings are invalid. Artifact bindings are {id} or {id,access}, without content hashes. FormationPin and the grant are runtime-attested metadata, not authored fields. Runtime rereads completed JSON and rejects invalid records.

2. Identity. The registry/interface folder is the only routing/policy identity. For isolation, author a new exact folder and permit it at every relevant policy layer. Code reuse imports implementation only. Labels, families, session lanes and binding aliases cannot select routes or grant authority.

3. Grant. Authority is worker-interface ceiling ∩ EE chain ∩ authored exact bindings. The initiator's grant does not clamp the new run. Choose an EE allowing the worker pin and required interfaces; extra bindings cannot widen authority.

4. Provider. Bind an exact system_worker_* pin and provider interface through checkpoints. A task-scoped provider can reuse code, but stays run-agnostic: run_authoring_profile names only the authoring tool/labels/timeout. Obtain run, worker, checkpoint, EE, epoch and provider coordinates from attested invocation metadata and the live record, never reverse ownership in provider config. Model/reasoning choices belong to interface policy/config. Authentication and state stay private to that provider.

5. Directions. Task input binds its source and routes to the provider. Provider output binds the provider and routes artifacts to authored receivers. Provider progression needs a granted file-tool door with separate authoring-call/result checkpoints. Other tools likewise have separate provider-output and tool-result edges.

6. Context. Bind role, grounding, instructions and prior results as {id} artifact_bindings at every checkpoint needing them. Interfaces materialize content-addressed refs. A tool-less run has no model-visible door. Provider-native compaction changes only private provider history and continues the same turn/run, with evidence. A separate compactor may return an explicit summary to the original run; it does not replace that run.

7. Return. Route output through an exact outbound interface. Receivers needing proof author required_verified_artifacts; runtime records a mark after the verifier passes. An unmet requirement is recorded data, not a blocking process or lease.

8. Addressed send. Use artifact.send when the model must choose an address. The exact target must be in the active bindings and formed grant; the artifact must satisfy every matching artifact policy. The result is admitted {seq} or a typed refusal. A reader may consume admitted output later; the send result is not its reply.
description: Author run records, checkpoint routes, context bindings and addressed artifact sends.
